Choose a new table name; do not replace customer data.'); return [{json:table}];

const rows=$input.all().filter(x=>x.json.id!==undefined); if(rows.length>1) throw new Error('Duplicate mutex rows need manual reconciliation.'); if(rows.length===1 && rows[0].json.sourceRef!=='folderit-ledger/v1') throw new Error('Unexpected lock schema.'); return [{json:{exists:rows.length?'yes':'no',tableId:$('Setup: Create or reuse ledger').first().json.id}}];

return [{json:{ledgerTableId:$('Setup: Create or reuse ledger').first().json.id, note:'Copy this ID into Settings in the customer workflows. Setup never resets an existing lock. Run setup once, not concurrently.'}}];

parameters.content:
# Send Folderit document due-date reminders to Microsoft Teams with saved receipts

Contract and certificate owners who maintain renewal dates in Folderit.

Read standard Folderit Due dates, calculate the current reminder milestone, and send one confirmed notice per document/date/milestone/destination.

**Folderit Tailor plan with API access is required.** Install `n8n-nodes-folderit` and use the standard-cloud OAuth2 credential. Requires Data Table node v1.1. Core processing was tested on n8n 2.42.5; test your real mailbox/channel before activation. The default export is inactive and contains no credentials or pinned results.

[Folderit installation and connection guide](https://www.folderit.com/knowledge-base/connect-folderit-to-n8n/)

![Workflow overview](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/folderit-dms/n8n-nodes-folderit/main/templates/assets/remind-teams-about-due-dates.png)

# Configure before activation

1. Keep this workflow inactive. Create credentials in n8n's credential store.
2. Run the separate **1. Set up receipt table** manual branch once, without running the service trigger. Run setup one at a time in the SAME n8n project.
3. Open **Copy ledgerTableId into Settings** and copy its `ledgerTableId`.
4. Select the SAME **Folderit OAuth2 API** credential in both Folderit read nodes. Enter accountUid, folderUid, teamId and channelId in **Settings**. Select a delegated **Microsoft Teams OAuth2** credential in the send node. Set reminderDays and overdueDays as needed. Paste ledgerTableId from the manual setup branch into Settings.
5. All copies processing the same source/destination must share the same table. Setup reuses an existing table of that name and preserves receipts. Keep its name stable.
6. Complete the acceptance checks, then activate the service trigger. Never put passwords, API secrets or tokens in Settings.

## Dates and reminders
Set each test document's standard Folderit **Due date**. This workflow does not extract dates from content, read arbitrary custom metadata, or decide legal expiry. Folderit records are only read. The folder scan is not recursive.

The schedule is 09:00 UTC; comparisons use UTC calendar days. Default milestones are 30, 7, 1 and 0 days. At 20 days remaining, the 30-day milestone is sent; it does not send every missed milestone. The 0-day notice can be sent once through 7 days overdue. A changed Due date starts a new cycle. Missing dates are skipped; malformed dates fail visibly.

## Inspect before retrying
Each destination action first saves a pending receipt. A confirmed result marks it done. A repeated input checks that receipt.

There is one shared processing lock, with **no automatic expiry**. A failed or uncertain action holds the lock. Uploads and Teams messages are never automatically retried.

1. Open the failed execution and confirm its owner has stopped.
2. Inspect the pending receipt and the actual Folderit file or Teams message.
3. If the action occurred, verify its exact identity; record its destination ID and mark only that receipt done.
4. Only after proving no action occurred and no old request can finish may you remove that pending receipt.
5. Reconcile all pending work before setting the lock free and its owner blank. Keep all completed receipts.
6. Retry the retained failed input. If the result is uncertain, keep it blocked.

Competing runs wait for the lock for about one minute. This is duplicate protection with manual recovery, not an exactly-once transaction. Keep failed executions/binaries long enough for recovery and monitor table quotas.

# Run this branch once

This branch creates or reuses the receipt table and validates its lock. It does not connect to Folderit or Microsoft and does not send mail.

Open **Ledger setup settings** and choose a stable table name, then execute **1. Set up receipt table**. Copy the final table ID into the main **Settings** node above. Do not run setup concurrently. Preserve this table when upgrading or duplicating the main workflow.

# Test your actual connections

Use synthetic documents with a future, due-today, overdue and missing Due date. Test invalid-date handling separately. Inspect each actual Teams message, then repeat the run and confirm that the same milestones are suppressed. Test a controlled channel-send failure. Keep the schedule off until all checks pass.

# Failure visibility and optional alerts

A failed action stops the run and can leave its receipt/lock pending. Inspect **Executions**, the receipt table and the actual destination before retrying. Keep failed-execution saving on.

For an email alert, import the [shared SMTP error workflow](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/folderit-dms/n8n-nodes-folderit/main/examples/folderit-failure-alert-email.json), configure its sender/recipient and SMTP credential, save it, then choose it in this workflow's **⋯ → Settings → Error workflow**. SMTP alerts are optional; core processing does not depend on that separate workflow.

Prove alert delivery with a controlled failure in an activated test workflow. Manual errors do not automatically invoke Error Trigger. An alert workflow can itself fail; monitor the provider separately.
